trust_decision.summary: The repository's proxy setting (repo.Proxy) is attacker-influenced configuration and must be rejected by an allowlist (scheme, hostname charset, numeric port) before it is interpolated into the shell-interpreted GIT_SSH_COMMAND ProxyCommand; the decision is enforced in util/git at credential-construction boundaries and again inside SSHCreds.Environ.

landing_point.why: The ProxyCommand is built by string interpolation of parsedProxyURL.Hostname()/Port() and the joined args are exported as GIT_SSH_COMMAND (util/git/creds.go:394), which git runs through a shell (the fix itself calls it a "shell-interpreted GIT_SSH_COMMAND string", fix.diff:134-135). The advisory names the SSH SOCKS5 proxy URL, so this line is where an engineer looks first.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: util/git/creds.go:417-418 (NewGitHubAppCreds) and util/git/creds.go:1041-1046 (AzureServicePrincipalCreds.WithProxy) - the same proxy-URL trust boundary implemented for the HTTP/HTTPS credential types, a different transport from the advisory's SSH command

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory's sink is the shell-interpreted GIT_SSH_COMMAND; GitHub App and Azure service-principal proxy URLs only feed net/http transports, so a solver can argue that validating them is unrelated hardening.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate authenticated SOCKS5 proxy (socks5://user:password@host:1080) must keep working: the userinfo must still become SOCKS5_USER/SOCKS5_PASSWD plus a usable ProxyCommand, and the returned closer must still delete the temporary SSH key file. An over-broad fix that rejects anything containing '@', drops all proxies, or stops emitting the SOCKS5_USER/SOCKS5_PASSWD env breaks authenticated proxy users.

O6_input_shapes: hostname containing a single quote plus command substitution: socks5://evil'$(id>/tmp/x)'host:1080
whitespace inside the hostname and control characters / newline in the port
wrong scheme for SSH (http, https, socks4) and rejected schemes for HTTP creds (socks4)
empty hostname, missing port, non-numeric port, port 0 and port 65536
IPv4 (socks5://127.0.0.1:1080), DNS name (socks5://proxy.example.com:1080), bracketed and full IPv6 (socks5://[::1]:1080)
socks5 and socks5h schemes for SSH; http/https/socks5/socks5h for HTTP creds
userinfo variants (user:password@host) that must still yield SOCKS5_USER/SOCKS5_PASSWD

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: that branch already parses the proxy and re-formats it itself as scheme://host:port, so a maintainer hardening proxy handling would plausibly copy the same validate-and-strip rule there; it is a different transport from the one the report names

O8b_injection_room.sibling: repo.Proxy passed straight to proxy.GetCallback for every HTTP/HTTPS git client, independent of the credential type (plain username/password repos never pass through the new checks)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix's own comment claims unsafe values cannot flow further "into net/http transports via GetRepoHTTPClient" (fix.diff:232-233), so a follow-up hardening would naturally add ValidateHTTPProxyURL at this lower-level entry

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the shared proxy callback accepting an arbitrary string via httpproxy.Config for git, helm and OCI clients (util/helm/client.go:410, util/oci/client.go:143)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: one shared helper is the obvious single place to enforce a proxy-URL allowlist, and it is reused by several transports

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a generated /bin/sh wrapper script on PATH with an unvalidated host:port interpolated into it (the same technique the fix adopts for SSH)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this repo already ships generated shell wrapper templates for git and helm, so a maintainer writing a proxy wrapper could do it without validating the URL first

O9_family: os_command_injection (CWE-78): untrusted repository proxy URL hostname/port interpolated into a shell-run GIT_SSH_COMMAND ProxyCommand
